name: Ash Plain
desc: A pyroclastic desert days after, under a sky that has not cleared — ash still falling out of the deck like snow, wind-worked dune fabric running to a dead horizon, lahar channels cut down through the fresh fall to the old dark surface, stripped timber standing buried to the knee, and a fissure off the horizon throwing a dull red on the underside of the cloud; everything is one material, and the fall never stops; cold grey ashfall, a warm ember night, sumi ink wash, a cyan survey sheet, or thermal false-colour.

energy.doc: how much light is left — the fissure glow on the cloud base, raking light on the dune crests, depth of the cloud shadow

scale.doc: size of the standing timber, the flakes and the dust devils — at max the near snags tower and the ash falls in gobbets

density.doc: how much is out there — dead trunks, falling ash, blowing veils, dust devils

speed.doc: how fast the deck rolls, the blanket advects and the ash comes down

fall.doc: how hard it is falling — flake size and count, and how much ash hangs in the air killing the horizon

hue.doc: the faint colour left in the ash; the fissure keys off it

x.doc: where the fissure sits beyond the horizon — the light rakes from that side

style.doc: aesthetic: cold grey ashfall under a dead sky — the ash, not the fire / an ember night, the fissure hot enough to colour the whole plain / sumi ink wash, the deck as a tonal wash and the timber as dry-brush / a cyan survey sheet of the fall and its channels / thermal false-colour, cold ash over a ground that still holds heat

seed.doc: fall lottery — dune fabric, channel network, where the timber stands
